statement: The clique adapter does four things. It parses the DIMACS binary graphs and the clique sizes the source publishes, shows the learner only the relabelled adjacency matrix, and evaluates answers. It contains no search, ranking, pruning or optimisation call, and nothing derived from a reference reaches the problem object. I wrote my own parser for this audit, sharing no code with the adapter. It reproduces the adapter's adjacency on all 56 graphs used, and its reference values and its 13 left-out graphs exactly: 50 values come from '[OPT = k]' in results.dmclique, c-fat500-10 from its solution file and the five gen graphs from their comment lines; no published statements disagree. The score is (k-1)/(reference-1) cut to [0,1] for a clique and 0 otherwise. It matched an independent exact evaluator on 948 answers across all 56 instances, and the problem's evaluate() and partial evaluation match the specification. All 39 cliques the source publishes score 1. Changing the stored references or the training flag changes nothing the learner can observe, and the seeded relabelling removes every order-based shortcut I tried. The kernel's split puts CFat, Kel, San and Stein in training, and 11 brock, 7 p_hat, 4 hamming and 2 johnson graphs in the 24 fresh ones. No group is shared, there are no duplicates across the two sides, and the anchor's baseline numbers reproduce. Four minor problems remain. (1) The scorer accepts ndarray subclasses, so a masked array is scored on its unmasked entries only. (2) The threshold counts trivially solved graphs at 1 only on sets made of hamming, johnson and p_hat graphs, so the bar on the hard graphs is 0.882 for brock on the deciding half and 0.90 for p_hat on the confirming half. (3) johnson8-2-4 in the deciding half is an induced subgraph of hamming8-4 in the confirming half. (4) The documentation miscounts the volume's duplicate files. None of these changes the score of any integer-array answer. The reference values are the source's and were not re-proved, though both fresh graphs without a published answer have their value reached in the pinned files. brock400_1 to brock400_3 share generator seed 0 and nested planted cliques, so the fresh brock graphs are not all independent draws.
coverage:
All scripts are in <scratch>/fresh/clique/audit2 (check.py with subcommands, mine.py, man.py, idx.py, dup.py, pre.py, t0.py). Each was run with nice -n 10 python3 -I, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 and ulimit -t 60, one at a time, about 25 CPU-seconds in total. Downloads are in audit2/dl and audit2/dl2, read as bytes or text only.

(1) I read every line of clique.py.

(2) My own reader of the binary format (Python-integer bit strings, high bit first, rows of i//8+1 bytes) on all 69 files:
- no diagonal or padding bit anywhere;
- the 1-bit count equals the p line everywhere except DSJC500.5 and DSJC1000.5, whose p lines are exactly twice the count;
- read low bit first, 67 of 69 files have bits on or above the diagonal;
- nodes and edges match contents.tex for every graph it lists;
- my adjacency equals the adapter's on all 56 used graphs;
- the 4 hamming and 4 johnson files equal the definitions in contents.tex, vertex k being the k-th vector.

(3) References, from my own token-based parsers of results.dmclique, results.dfmax, contents.tex, the solution files and the comment lines: same 56 used graphs, same values, same 13 left out, and claim lists identical to the adapter's for all 69 graphs.
- All 39 published cliques were checked under both numberings: 25 solution files read from 0 (they list vertex 0, although ccformat.tex says nodes are numbered from 1), 12 brock lists read from 0, 2 MANN lists read from 1. Each is a clique of exactly the reference size and scores 1.0; under the other numbering none is a clique.
- A bounded plateau probe reached the value on the two fresh graphs with no published answer, p_hat700-1 (11) and p_hat1000-1 (10).
- No simple rule found a clique larger than a published value on any graph.
- All 12 p_hat files carry the 23 September correction note.

(4) Evaluator agreement (checks 'agree' and 'all'), detailed in the agreement field.

(5) Privileged information (check 'leak'):
- On 8 instances I swapped in 3 fake references and rebuilt the problem with the same seed. The pickled view fields, the results of every view call and the adapter's internal fields were all unchanged.
- training=True and training=False give identical results; problem() never reads the flag.
- No exposed value equals the reference: the exposed values are only 0, 1, 2 and n.

(6) Order (check 'order'):
- I tried 10 rules that only work in the files' own order: the even-weight indices on hamming6-2 and hamming8-2, and the published clique at its raw indices on 8 graphs. Each scores 1.0 in raw labels and 0.0 under all 5 relabellings.
- The largest |correlation| between old and new index was 0.18.
- Two seeds give different orders; two instances of one size under one run seed are relabelled differently.

(7) Degenerate answers: 20 kinds on 3 instances, sent through run._valid and the kernel's scoring path.

(8) The generic kernel checks that do not involve the learner: one layout over 56 instances, the view hides the adapter, arrays are read-only, assignment is metered, the malformed list of test_kernel is refused, and the same raw clique scores the same under 4 relabellings.

(9) Split and halves: split(env,16,24), halves(), threshold_for. Cross-side near-duplicates were tested by (n, edges), degree sequences and edge overlap in raw labels; the overlaps equal what independent random graphs of those densities give. I also checked the stated effect of putting san1000 in SanR (as documented) and instruct.tex's "Sanchis graphs" line for gen*.

(10) Anchor: I recomputed random maximal clique (20 orders) and greedy (5 runs). I also scored minimum-degree peeling (fresh 0.714, half A 0.653, half B 0.786) and static-degree greedy (0.693 / 0.692 / 0.694); neither is near any threshold.

(11) Manifest: 104 entries equal the 104 files on disk and every SHA-256 matches.
- Re-fetched results.dmclique, contents.tex, brock800_1.clq.b and SOLUTIONS/c-fat500-10.sol: identical.
- Fetched 5 volume copies (p_hat300-1, p_hat700-3, brock200_2, keller4, MANN_a27): byte-identical to the benchmarks/clique files.
- Confirmed the http address returns a 301 redirect to the https one.
- The challenge, graph, clique and volume index pages contain no licence or terms text, and the gen_info.tex quote is verbatim (lines 168-170).

Not checked:
- optimality of any reference value;
- bin2asc.c (code, not fetched); the bit layout is supported by the data checks above instead;
- 18 of the 23 volume copies;
- the process claims that the threshold and size rule were fixed before any learner result;
- the learner, which was not run or imported;
- the audit1, fix1 and work directories (outside the allowed scope).

findings.title: Scorer accepts ndarray subclasses: a masked array is scored on its unmasked entries
findings.problem: Clique.score and decode test isinstance(answer, np.ndarray), so subclasses get through. For a numpy MaskedArray, np.all((a==0)|(a==1)) and np.flatnonzero(a==1) skip masked entries. run._valid checks the raw data (well_formed calls np.asarray, which drops the mask), but the adapter scores only the unmasked part, so the answer validated and the answer scored are different vectors. This contradicts the module's statement that anything that is not an integer array of 0s and 1s of length n scores 0 'no conversion, nothing repaired'. It gives no gain beyond a clique the learner already had to find, hence minor.
findings.evidence: check.py degenerate: on brock200_1 (reference 21), np.ma.array(all ones, mask = every vertex outside a 15-clique) gives _valid=True and kernel-path score 0.7, the score of the unmasked 15-clique. The all-ones vector itself scores 0.0. Same on hamming6-4 and johnson8-2-4 (1.0). The other 19 degenerate kinds score 0 or their correct value: empty, single vertex, all ones, bool, float, list, object, shape (n,1), n+1 or n-1 entries, a 2, a -1, NaN, None, 0-d array, uint8, int8, non-contiguous view.
findings.fix: In Clique.problem.decode use `if type(answer) is not np.ndarray or answer.shape != perm.shape: return answer`. In Clique.score use `if type(a) is not np.ndarray or a.shape != (len(inst['adjacent']),) or a.dtype.kind not in 'iu' or not np.all((a == 0) | (a == 1)): return 0.0`. The kernel's run._valid has the same isinstance test; that is outside this adapter.

findings.title: threshold_for counts trivially solved graphs at 1 only on hamming/johnson/p_hat-only sets, so the bar on the hard graphs differs between sets
findings.problem: On the confirming half the hamming graphs are counted at 1, so its threshold is 0.936 and the p_hat graphs need 0.90. On the deciding half the two johnson graphs, which score 1 for every maximal clique, are not counted at 1, so the threshold stays 0.90 and the 11 brock graphs need only 0.882. On the whole fresh set (threshold 0.90) the 18 graphs other than hamming and johnson need 0.867. The anchor states the two half figures, so nothing is hidden. But the run record carries only the number (0.90 or 0.936), and a pass on A and a pass on B read as the same bar are not. The anchor's own numbers reproduce.
findings.evidence: check.py split: half A (11 Bro + 2 Joh) threshold 0.9; half B (4 Ham + 7 PHat) threshold 0.9364. check.py baselines: brock mean needed for half A at 0.90 with johnson at 1 is 0.8818; greedy (5 runs) on hamming and johnson is 1.0 in every run; random maximal clique on both johnson graphs is 1.0. check.py generic: johnson8-2-4 has 105 maximal cliques, all of size 4. Whole fresh set: (0.9*24 - 6)/18 = 0.867.
findings.fix: If no learner result on this category has been scored yet, apply the same rule to every set: in threshold_for drop the condition `set(groups) <= set(CONFIRMING)` and return threshold + (1 - threshold) * (share of groups in AT_MAXIMUM). That gives half A 0.9154, the whole fresh set 0.925, and half B unchanged at 0.9364. Otherwise leave the rule and add to `anchor` the demand on the non-trivial graphs of each set (half A 0.882, half B 0.90, whole fresh set 0.867).

findings.title: Cross-half sibling: johnson8-2-4 (deciding half) is an induced subgraph of hamming8-4 (confirming half)
findings.problem: halves() is meant to keep instances that share data or a generator in one half. The family codes Joh and Ham are separate groups, so they land in different halves, yet both come from the same contributor's generator (contents.tex: 'see the generator in graph/contributed/pardalos'). johnson8-2-4 is exactly hamming8-4 restricted to its weight-2 vectors. The module text does not say so. It has no practical effect here, because every maximal clique of johnson8-2-4 scores 1 and the pair cannot carry a decision into its confirmation.
findings.evidence: check.py split: 'johnson8-2-4 (half A) == hamming8-4 (half B) induced on weight-2 vectors: True'. check.py defs: both files equal the contents.tex definitions with vertex k the k-th vector.
findings.fix: Add one sentence to the module docstring: johnson8-2-4 (deciding half) is the subgraph of hamming8-4 (confirming half) induced on its 28 weight-2 vectors, from the same generator, and every maximal clique of it scores 1. Do not merge the groups: group() also drives split() and merging would change the training/fresh split.

findings.title: Documentation miscounts the volume's duplicate graphs
findings.problem: The module docstring and the manifest's source field say 'the volume's 16 other graphs are byte-identical copies of files of benchmarks/clique'. In fact benchmarks/volume/Clique lists 37 graphs: 11 fetched, 3 neither fetched nor copies (C2000.5, C2000.9, C4000.5, above the size rule) and 23 that are also in benchmarks/clique. 16 of those are within the size rule; 7 are above it (MANN_a45, MANN_a81, hamming10-4, keller6, p_hat1500-1, p_hat1500-2, p_hat1500-3).
findings.evidence: idx.py on the fetched listing of https://archive.dimacs.rutgers.edu/pub/challenge/graph/benchmarks/volume/Clique/: 38 entries including Appendix.tex. The 5 copies fetched (p_hat300-1, p_hat700-3, brock200_2, keller4, MANN_a27) have SHA-256 equal to the benchmarks/clique files.
findings.fix: Write: 'the volume's 23 graphs that are also in benchmarks/clique (16 of them within the size rule) are byte-identical copies of those files and are not fetched; C2000.5, C2000.9 and C4000.5 are above the size rule'. Use the same wording in the manifest's source field and the module docstring.

evaluator_agreement:
My evaluator: my own parser of the files, my own reference parse, my own decoding by the documented rule (perm = default_rng(seed).permutation(n), perm[new] = old) and an exact Fraction score.

Answers compared: 500 answers on 10 instances (johnson8-2-4, MANN_a9, hamming6-2, keller4, brock200_2, san400_0.7_1, c-fat500-10, brock800_1, p_hat1000-1, san1000), of which 406 valid cliques, including empty, single-vertex and two-vertex ones, random sub-cliques and random maximal cliques, and 94 invalid answers. Plus 448 answers covering all 56 instances. Across these 948 answers three things agreed exactly, with a largest difference of 0.0:
- env.score(i, decode(a));
- my exact score;
- the view's evaluate() totals, compared with my own counts [-k, chosen non-adjacent pairs].
Also, valid if and only if group 1 is 0, and score equals clip((-tot[0]-1)/(reference-1)).

Partial evaluation: 6 random partial constructions on each of the 10 instances. At every step candidates() equals the difference of partial_totals() for both options, and totals() after assign() equals partial_totals(). The fast rows equal the slow default rows on 40-variable batches that include assigned vertices, and the totals equal my own count.

Exposed array: on all 56 instances the view's var_var[0] equals my own adjacency permuted by the documented rule.

Reference values: my own parse equals the adapter's on all 56 used graphs and gives the same 13 left out.

Published answers: the source publishes 39, and each is a clique of exactly the reference size that scores 1.0. For the other graphs the source publishes values only; for the two fresh ones (p_hat700-1, p_hat1000-1) the value was reached in the pinned files by a bounded probe.
exposed:
Everything below was read from AssignView on all 56 instances.
- var_var[0] (n x n float, symmetric, zero diagonal, values 0/1): the adjacency matrix taken from the file's binary block (lower triangle, row i = pairs (i,j) with j<i, first bit = high bit of the first byte, rows padded to i//8+1 bytes), symmetrised, with rows and columns permuted by the seed. On all 56 instances it equals my own parse under perm = default_rng(seed).permutation(n). It is the only field of the file shown, besides n (NODES of the p line).
- var_attr (n x 0) and opt_attr (2 x 0): empty. opt_opt, var_opt and occ_attr: empty tuples.
- capacity None, domain None, start_answer None, start_totals None, ordered False, n_opts 2 (option 0 = out, option 1 = in; options are not relabelled), n_groups 2.
- Groups, traced to gen_info.tex ('a clique ... is a set of pairwise adjacent nodes'; maximum = most vertices). Group 0 (soft) is minus the number of vertices given option 1. Group 1 (hard) is the number of chosen pairs not joined by an edge. hard = [False, True], detail = [False, False].
- Not exposed: comment lines (they list the planted clique for brock and MANN and state the size for san, gen and keller), names, edge counts, reference values.

Design decisions, said plainly:
- Free order, no capacity, every vertex set is an answer, a clique exactly when group 1 is 0.
- Because the hard group counts conflicting pairs, candidates() gives for each unchosen vertex [-1, the number of chosen vertices it is not adjacent to]; for a chosen vertex, option 0 gives [+1, minus that count]. This is the exact change of the specified totals, as the generic form requires, not an extra hint. It is, however, exactly the add/swap information clique local search is built on, at 2 units per vertex. The interface cannot remove a vertex, so improving a complete answer costs full constructions or evaluations of n units each.
- The full adjacency lets the learner compute degrees and other graph statistics unmetered.
- The zero point is a single vertex, so on graphs with small references (johnson8-2-4 and hamming6-4 at 4, p_hat300-1 at 8) one vertex is worth 1/3 to 1/7 of the scale.
- The family choices (san1000 kept in San, gen* put in San) decide which graphs are fresh: with san1000 in SanR, p_hat500-1 would leave the fresh set and both johnson graphs would move to the confirming half (checked).
- 6 of the 24 fresh graphs score 1 under greedy in every run (hamming) or under any maximal clique (johnson).
